question: How are the half-measure bindu and the obstructing power defined in this cosmology?
premises: The bindu is remembered as half-measure and has the form of space.
The half-moon is half of that bindu, and the obstructing power is an eighth part of it.
inference: The text defines a descending sequence of subtle levels from the half-measure bindu to the obstructing power by form and proportion.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'its' in the proportional compound is compressed and could be read in more than one way.
plain_english: The bindu is called the half-measure and is said to have the form of space with four parts. Half of that is the half-moon, and by an eighth part of it comes the obstructing power.
